correctness.rationale: The three forms have no common zero, and on the affine chart the projection is t↦t^n. For every nontrivial n-th root ζ, x(t)−x(ζt) is a nonzero rational function, so Galois correspondence gives birationality and the degree is n+2. The two poles ±i meet transversely at P. With k=(n+1)/2 odd and w=t², expanding the cross-product gives the displayed Qζ(w). Neither 0 nor −1 is a root; the other potential denominator value w=−ζ⁻² gives Qζ(w)=−2(1+ζ)/ζ≠0. A multiple root forces |1+ζ|=(k−1)^(k−1)/k^k<1/k, whereas the root-of-unity separation is at least 2/n>1/k. Subtracting Qζ and Qη in a purported triple forces w=−1. Thus all k(n−1) affine double points are transverse, counted by dividing the ordered collision pairs by two. At infinity the first local coordinate is a² times a unit in a², while the second is a^n; absorbing the unit gives an A_{n−1} cusp. The delta sum is n(n+1)/2, exhausting the arithmetic genus. The unique cusp forces an affine lift; invariance of the base-point-free section space forces b=0 from the missing degree n+1 and a²=1 from its degree-two subspace. For a degree-q Cremona map with base multiplicities m_i, the degree formula and ∑m_i=3(q−1) bound the image degree below by d+(q−1)(d−6), since the curve has multiplicity at most two also at infinitely near points. Thus preservation forces q=1. The odd cyclic deck group intersects the two-element projective stabilizer trivially.
